beats: Hook: four knives, one cake: cut a training job by the batch, by the sentence, by the layers, or inside each layer (line_split_cake_knives).
Only two things to cut: the data and the model (her words, slide 22-23).
One GPU: a batch of sentences flows through layers 0-3, one chef runs every station (slide 23) (line_split_one_chef_line).
Data parallel: split the batch; copy the whole kitchen, each copy cooks part of the orders (slide 24) (line_split_twin_kitchens).
Context parallel: split each sequence along its length, for very long documents (slide 25) (line_split_long_roll, line_long_ribbon).
Pipeline parallel: split the layers; an assembly line, one station per chef (slide 26) (line_split_assembly).
Tensor parallel: split inside each layer; two chefs share one huge step (slide 27) (line_split_big_pizza).
MoE aside (her question): expert parallelism cuts the model into experts and, as a result, cuts the data dynamically, unevenly; the four classic cuts are static (line_split_expert_stations).

Takeaway: 4D: every GPU is one coordinate (DP, CP, PP, TP) and holds one shard of data and one shard of model (slide 28) (line_split_kitchen_block, line_split_slices_plates); the map for the next episodes (line_course_map).
